unit_text: the brigade (Garrard, after the fall of Weed)

window.part_of_day: during the night
window.note: "At night" after the fight of 2 July (the paragraph runs from the afternoon of the 2d to "The next day the brigade remained in the same position"): the night of 2-3 July, from sunset to sunrise by the project ephemeris; no hour of the work

place.text: Round Top ridge (Little Round Top), about half way down the slope in front of the brigade's line, "wherever the rocks offered no protection"

tier_basis: The passage is in the passive voice ("this ridge ... was strengthened by building a stone wall"): it does not name who built it. It stands in the report of the brigade that held the ridge, after the account of how its four regiments took post, and the brigade remained there; the regimental accounts (91st Pennsylvania, 140th and 146th New York) name their regiments as builders, but this row rests on the brigade report alone, so the attribution to the brigade is reasoned.
quote: At night this ridge, naturally strong, was strengthened by building a stone wall about half way down the slope, wherever the rocks offered no protection to theinen.
notes: The principal source for E-14 / S-043 in the Official Records: a stone wall built at night about half way down the slope of Round Top ridge, wherever the rocks gave no protection. Fisher (Pennsylvania Reserves) has a stone wall thrown up "across the entire ravine and up the hill" in the morning of the 3d; a veteran of the 1st Pennsylvania Reserves (1892, quoted by the park) has the breastworks in front of the 16th Michigan built on the night of 3 July: conflict C-E14-TIME. Tools, men and length of the wall are not stated.

unit_text: Hazlett's battery (Battery D, Fifth U. S. Artillery)

window.part_of_day: after about 4 p. m., the brigade moving forward at the double-quick
window.note: "until about 4 p. m. At this time the brigade was moved rapidly forward"; the battery "ascended the ridge ... and went into battery on the summit" after the leading regiment: no hour; the report has Hazlett mortally wounded "A few moments after" Weed (Rittenhouse in Martin's report: died at 8 p. m.), so the end is the day bound

place.text: Round Top ridge (Little Round Top): up the slope behind the 140th New York to the summit

tools_props.item: the guns of Battery D, Fifth U. S. Artillery

quote: Hazlett's battery ascended the ridge immediately in rear of this regiment
context_quote: lying by their arms until about 4 p. m. At this time the brigade was moved rapidly forward (most of the time at the double-quick)
notes: Garrard says the battery "ascended the ridge immediately in rear of" the 140th New York "and went into battery on the summit"; he does not say how the guns were brought up (by teams or by hand) nor that any works were made (EG-LIFE-0402). The accounts of the 155th Pennsylvania and the 140th New York put the guns up by hand and handspike (state volumes, conflict C-G06-HAULING). The clip is a stand-in for the gun teams.

unit_text: Anderson's brigade of Georgia troops (Hood's division)

window.part_of_day: between the fight of 2 July and the charge of the Reserves at 5 o'clock on the 3d
window.note: the report puts the Reserves' charge "At 5 o'clock on the 3d" (afternoon: the enemy battery "established ... at noon" was in front); the wall was made stronger before it, after the Confederate attack of the 2d: the start is the sunset bound of 2 July, the end the stated 5 o'clock

place.text: the woods beyond the wheat-field (Rose's Woods): "a stone wall running through the woods"

quote: It had taken position behind a stone wall running through the woods, and which they had made stronger by rails and logs.
context_quote: At 5 o'clock on the 3d, I received orders from General Sykes, commanding the corps, to advance that portion of my command
notes: A Confederate improvement of a field wall, seen by the Union attackers of 3 July: rails and logs added to a stone wall "running through the woods". The report does not say which wall; the nearest pre-existing wall of PDF B.7.3 is P-04 (between Rose's Woods and the Wheatfield), named here for the marking rule, not by the report. Anderson's Georgia brigade (the 15th Georgia lost its colors there) is the unit the report names.

unit_text: the three brigades of Hood's division (Anderson, Robertson, Benning), "They"

window.part_of_day: after the Reserves' charge of 5 o'clock
window.note: after "At 5 o'clock on the 3d" the charge that routed the three brigades; "They fell back nearly a mile to a second ridge, and intrenched themselves": no hour, so the end is the day bound

place.text: a second ridge nearly a mile back from the wall (the Confederate right, west of the wheat-field)

quote: They fell back nearly a mile to a second ridge, and intrenched themselves.
context_quote: At 5 o'clock on the 3d, I received orders from General Sykes, commanding the corps, to advance that portion of my command
notes: Crawford: after the Reserves' charge the enemy "fell back nearly a mile to a second ridge, and intrenched themselves"; McCandless (R219): the enemy "were busy during the night chopping timber and fortifying" on a wooded ridge about half a mile in advance of his front. Whether these are the Confederate works the register names (W-CONFED-WARFIELD-WORKS) is not stated by either report.

unit_text: the division (Lieutenant Harding, ordnance officer)

window.note: "On the 4th"; no hour

context_quote: and upward of 7,000 stand of arms
notes: The captured arms of the 2d and 3d (Enfield, Springfield, Austrian and other rifles, 3,672 listed in the return of 4 July) were collected under the division's ordnance officer; "Large piles of these arms were found on brush heaps, ready to be burned" (the enemy's). Men and tools not stated; the pose is a stand-in (carrying bulky loads in pairs).

unit_text: the enemy (read as Hood's division, Crawford R218)

window.part_of_day: during the night
window.note: "On the evening of the 3d instant" the advance; the enemy "were busy during the night": the night of 3-4 July, from sunset to sunrise by the project ephemeris

place.text: a wooded ridge about half a mile in advance of McCandless's front (the Confederate right, west of the wheat-field)

tier_basis: McCandless writes "the enemy"; Crawford's report of the same action names the force on this front as "the division of Major-General Hood" and says it "intrenched" on "a second ridge": the unit is reasoned from that. The act (chopping timber and fortifying through the night) is stated.
quote: The enemy took up a new position on a wooded ridge about half a mile in advance of our front, and were busy during the night chopping timber and fortifying.
notes: Confederate field works of the night of 3-4 July seen from the Union picket line; no timber count, men or length stated.

unit_text: my men (the two regiments of the brigade that had not gone up the hill)

window.part_of_day: in the morning
window.note: "In the morning I discovered that the hill was of immense importance ... so I changed my position ... and at once threw up a stone wall": the morning of 3 July; no hour is stated

place.text: across the entire ravine between Little Round Top and Round Top and up the hill (the saddle between the two hills)

quote: so I changed my position, throwing the left flank of the two regiments which had not gone up the hill around so as to completely cover the ravine between the two hills, and at once threw up a stone wall across the entire ravine and up the hill, thus giving my men a sure protection against any advance which could possibly have been inade by the enemy
context_quote: In the morning I discovered that the hill was of immense importance to us
notes: Colonel Fisher: after the 10 p. m. ascent of Round Top by the Fifth and Twelfth Pennsylvania Reserves and the 20th Maine, he moved the other two regiments of his brigade (the Eleventh was with McCandless) and "at once threw up a stone wall across the entire ravine and up the hill". Time: the morning of the 3d here; the night of 2 July in Garrard's report (Weed's brigade, half way down the slope); the night of 3 July in a veteran's letter of 1892 (conflict C-E14-TIME). Tools, men and length not stated.

unit_text: my battery (Battery L, First Ohio Light Artillery, Capt. Gibbs)

window.part_of_day: about the middle of the afternoon
window.note: "About the middle of the afternoon an orderly came rapidly up, asking our battery to come to the assistance of the Fifth Corps": no hour of the placing is stated

place.text: the valley below Little Round Top: the left section on the left of a road leading from the valley, on the right slope of Little Round Top ("Weed's Hill"); the center and right sections on the right of the road

tools_props.item: the guns of the battery (light 12-pounders), unhitched from their teams

quote: The rocky nature of the ground compelled us to unhitch our horses and place our guns in position by hand
context_quote: About the middle of the afternoon an orderly came rapidly up, asking our battery to come to the assistance of the Fifth Corps.
x_record_owner_note: record placed by report_assignments.json with another group; the report is a Fifth Corps report (request note bt-life-us-5c-reassign-records)
notes: Documented hand-placing of guns on 2 July: the ground was too rocky for teams, so the horses were unhitched and the guns put in position "by hand" (the section chiefs Guthrie, Gildea and Walworth). This is Battery L, not Hazlett's Battery D (G-06), which stood on the summit; the 155th Pennsylvania and 140th New York accounts say Hazlett's guns were hauled up by hand (state volumes). No works, platform or earth is mentioned for any gun. Men and how many hands not stated.

quote: continued its march toward Gettysburg, halting after midnight about 2 miles from that place. Resuming its march, after a brief rest of two or three hours, the division reached Gettysburg at about 7 o'clock in the morning of Jidy 3.

unit_text: the division (Barnes)

The date of this row is therefore reasoned from the chain of the same report, not read from the line.
quote: The command here rested for further instructions. After the lapse of an hour or more, the division received orders to change its position, moving some distance to the rear and toward the left of this first line

notes: "The command here rested for further instructions" at the first position; later "we were held in reserve in an orchard on the left of the road, with instructions to wait there for further orders ... These various movements occupied the time until long after midday." A day of waiting in reserve; no meal, fire or camp work is stated.
